description: How a config.json object's mapping subtree loads, and whether the file must be copied to config.pre-profiles.json before the next save rewrites it (DESIGN v2.4 B and C, ADR 0006). deviceMappings wins when it is an object, even an empty one; it decodes tolerantly per entry: a profile whose value is not an object is dropped, and a binding that is not an action is dropped, the rest kept. When deviceMappings is absent or not an object, a legacy button-keyed mapping migrates losslessly into the dualsense profile, provided it is an object whose every key is a DualSense control id and every value an action; otherwise the defaults apply. backupBeforeSave is true when deviceMappings is present and anything in it would not decode exactly (a non-object counts, null included), or when deviceMappings is absent and the legacy mapping key is present (any value, null included). Input is a config.json object; expected is {deviceMappings, backupBeforeSave}. Mappings are written {profileID: {controlID: <action descriptor>}}, or the string "defaults" for the shipped default mappings.
function: AppConfig.init(from:) mapping subtree and ConfigStore.backupConfigBeforeLossyLoadIfNeeded(at:data:) — input a config.json object, expected {deviceMappings, backupBeforeSave}
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.4 B and C; Tests/PowerUpTests/MappingFixtureTests.swift testConfigLoadTable decodes AppConfig from the input and compares deviceMappings, then writes the input to a temporary config.json, calls ConfigStore.backupConfigBeforeLossyLoadIfNeeded and checks that config.pre-profiles.json exists exactly when backupBeforeSave is true; both ask the core through the bridge since slice 2.2. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/mapping.rs config_load_cases runs mapping::load_device_mappings on the input text, and rust/powerup-core/tests/config.rs config_load_cases_through_the_config_decoder runs config::load_config on it, the JSONDecoder reading in front of the mapping layer included.

cases.reason: The default config as the app writes it holds nothing the next save would lose.

cases.name: neither key gives the defaults
cases.reason: A config from before mappings existed, or a hand-trimmed one, gets the shipped layout (HK-013); there is nothing to lose, so no copy.

cases.name: an empty config gives the defaults
cases.reason: An empty object is a valid config with every key defaulted.

cases.name: a legacy mapping migrates losslessly into dualsense
cases.reason: Pre-ADR-0006 button-keyed mappings move into the DualSense profile unchanged, sendPrompt and an explicit none included; the next save rewrites the file in the new shape, so the original is copied first (HK-014).

cases.name: the new key wins when both are present
cases.reason: deviceMappings is the truth once written; the stale legacy key is ignored, and a deviceMappings that decodes fully is not copied (HK-013).

cases.name: an empty deviceMappings wins over a legacy mapping
cases.reason: An object, even an empty one, is the new shape; the user unbound everything on purpose.

cases.name: an empty deviceMappings means no bindings
cases.reason: No bindings is a choice the user made, not a missing value: it is not replaced by the defaults and not copied.

cases.name: an unknown action drops only that binding
cases.reason: Tolerant per entry (HK-011): an action from a newer build costs that one binding, never the profile or the tree; the next save drops it, so the file is copied first.

cases.name: a profile that is not an object is dropped alone
cases.reason: A malformed profile drops only itself (HK-011).

cases.name: a profile that is an array is dropped alone
cases.reason: A profile's mapping is keyed by control id; an array is not a mapping.

cases.name: a null profile is dropped alone
cases.reason: null is not a mapping either; the other profiles stay.

cases.name: a null binding is dropped alone
cases.reason: A null action is not none; it is dropped, and the file is copied before the save forgets it.

cases.name: an action with an unknown sibling key is kept and not backed up
cases.reason: Quirk kept knowingly: Swift's decoder cannot see a key that is not a case, so the binding loads and the strict check passes; the next save writes {"approve":{}} and the sibling is lost without a copy.

cases.name: a null deviceMappings falls back to the legacy mapping
cases.reason: Only an object wins; a null new key does not hide a legacy mapping, and the file is copied because the save rewrites both keys.

cases.name: a string deviceMappings falls back to the legacy mapping
cases.reason: A deviceMappings of the wrong type is ignored, like any mistyped key.

cases.name: a null deviceMappings alone gives the defaults
cases.reason: Nothing usable is left, so the defaults apply; the key was present, so the file is copied before the save replaces it.

cases.name: an array deviceMappings alone gives the defaults
cases.reason: An array is not the new shape; the defaults apply and the file is copied.

cases.name: a legacy mapping with an unknown action resets to the defaults
cases.reason: Quirk kept knowingly (HK-012): the legacy mapping is all or nothing, unlike deviceMappings; the original is still copied.

cases.name: a legacy mapping with an unknown button resets to the defaults
cases.reason: Legacy keys must be DualSense control ids; anything else fails the whole legacy mapping.

cases.name: an empty legacy mapping migrates to an empty dualsense profile
cases.reason: An empty legacy mapping is still a mapping: the DualSense ends up with no bindings, not the defaults.

cases.name: a legacy array resets to the defaults
cases.reason: A legacy mapping of the wrong type gives the defaults (AppConfigTests.testWrongTypesFallBackToDefaults); the key is present, so the file is copied.

cases.name: a null legacy mapping gives the defaults
cases.reason: A null legacy key gives the defaults, yet still counts as present for the copy.
